title: Want big arms? Get an arm day
summary: NH argues that maximal arm growth for naturals requires a dedicated arm day, treated as seriously as leg training. Compounds alone don't grow arms because they are secondary movers, and end-of-workout isolation is only a beginner's start. An arm day should open with an arm-friendly compound (close-grip bench, heavy rows) and progressively overload curls and extensions to heavy weights; it is low on CNS fatigue and can replace a rest day.

claims.claim: An arm day is a session whose only goal is training the arms; the fitness community resists it and treats arm work as something tacked on after the 'real' training.
People who only do arm isolation at the end of their workout usually have small arms; there is a correlation.
Natural lifters often have big legs because they train legs seriously with many squats, deadlifts and variations; the same logic should be applied to arms.

Approach 1, relying on main lifts (bench, close-grip bench, overhead press for triceps; chins and rows for biceps; deadlifts for forearms), doesn't grow arms for naturals unless genetically gifted, because the arms are only secondary movers.
Even in close-grip bench the chest and shoulders move the weight, and a chin-up mostly works the back because of the angle and gravity.
Approach 2, isolation after the main lift (extensions after bench, curls after rows), is the best start for beginners who have never trained arms, but it only takes you so far.
To maximise arm hypertrophy you need an arm day; this is only necessary if big arms are your goal.
An arm day is not hours of curls; sneak in compound lifts that benefit the arms and overall strength, e.g. open with close-grip bench before triceps isolation, or a heavy row before curls.
Big arms require moving big weight: curling 50 lb gives the arms no reason to grow, just as legs wouldn't grow from squatting 225 lb for five years.
Build curl strength gradually, as with the big lifts: start with something like 10 lb per side on an EZ bar for sets of 5-6 and add weight week after week.
The day you curl an EZ bar with 45 lb plates on each side with proper form, you will have big arms.
Curls, extensions and wrist curls are not taxing on the central nervous system, so an arm day can replace a rest day before a big session; the blood flow also aids recovery.
NH's arms are 18 inches pumped and 17.5 inches cold, which he cites as grounds to speak on the topic.
The biggest biceps in the gym usually belong to 'bros' who curl heavy every day, not powerlifters or weightlifters; learn from them rather than snubbing them. That is how NH built his arms.
